title: Voyager 1 Will Soon Be One Light-Day From Earth
summary:
NASA launched Voyager 1 in 1977. It was supposed to last just five years. Almost 50 years later, it is still working!

Voyager 1 zooms through space at about 38,000 miles per hour. If it stays on course, it will be one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026. A light-day is how far light travels in one day, about 16 billion miles. No human-made object has ever been that far away.

Voyager 1 first studied Jupiter and Saturn. It sent back pictures of their rings and moons. Then it kept going. In 2012, it entered interstellar space, the area far beyond the Sun.

Its power source is slowly making less electricity. To save energy, NASA engineers have turned off some of its tools. On April 17, 2026, they shut off one that measured charged particles. Two tools still work.

NASA hopes Voyager 1 can keep sending information for many more years.
why_it_matters: Voyager 1 shows that well-built machines can explore far into space and teach us about places no one can visit.
